memory: I have been on various medications over the years to manage my health conditions, including diabetes, hypertension, osteoarthritis, and hypothyroidism. I have had to adjust my medication regimen a few times to find what works best for me. To ensure I don't miss any doses or mix up any prescriptions, I keep track of everything using a medication list. My doctor and I review my medication list every few months to see if any adjustments are needed. It is crucial to stay on top of my medication management to maintain my overall health and well-being.I have been taking metformin 1000 mg twice daily for several years to manage my Type 2 Diabetes. It has been effective in keeping my blood sugar in check, but my A1C has remained around 6.9%. To further improve control, my doctor suggested adding a GLP-1 receptor agonist, semaglutide(Ozempic), at a low dose. I have noticed that it helps control my appetite, which is a welcome bonus. Additionally, I regularly check my fasting blood sugar at home, and it typically ranges between 125-130 mg/dL.I have been taking losartan 50 mg once daily to manage my high blood pressure. While my readings have been mostly in the 135-140/80-90 mmHg range, which is slightly higher than ideal, my doctor suggests that stress management and reducing sodium intake could help bring the numbers down without the need for a dosage increase. Additionally, I take a daily magnesium supplement, which has been shown to have a beneficial effect on blood pressure regulation.I have been taking levothyroxine 75 mcg every morning to manage my hypothyroidism. It has been stable for years, and my last TSH test came back at 2.1 mIU/L, which is within the normal range. To ensure optimal absorption, I take it on an empty stomach and wait at least 30 minutes before eating. Missing a dose can cause me to feel sluggish the next day, so I use a pill organizer to stay on track.I have been taking acetaminophen as needed for mild pain associated with osteoarthritis. However, when my joints are particularly stiff, my doctor prescribed meloxicam 7.5 mg, an anti-inflammatory, which provides significant relief. I only take it when necessary to avoid overusing NSAIDs. Additionally, my doctor suggested trying glucosamine supplements, but I'm not sure if they've made a noticeable difference in my symptoms.I recently had to adjust my vitamin D intake after my last blood test showed that my levels were low at 22 ng/mL, which is below the normal range of above 30 ng/mL. To address this, I now take vitamin D3 2,000 IU daily. Additionally, my last bone density scan indicated early signs of osteopenia, so I also take calcium supplements. My doctor recommended combining it with vitamin K2 to enhance absorption.I have been taking atorvastatin 10 mg daily as a statin to help manage my cholesterol. My doctor prescribed it because my LDL levels were slightly high at 130 mg/dL, and my triglycerides were at 140 mg/dL. So far, my cholesterol numbers have been improving, and I haven't experienced any side effects, which is a relief since some people report muscle aches with statins.I take a daily multivitamin to ensure I'm getting all the necessary nutrients. Omega-3 supplements are also part of my routine to support heart health. Additionally, I take probiotics to help maintain a healthy digestive system. Since I had my gallbladder removed a few years ago, I sometimes need to take digestive enzymes after consuming heavier meals. It's important to be mindful of my diet and adjust accordingly to ensure smooth digestion.I am cautious about potential medication interactions, particularly with losartan and meloxicam. My doctor advised me to avoid taking meloxicam too frequently because NSAIDs can affect kidney function. Additionally, I ensure that I take my thyroid medication separately from my calcium and iron supplements, as they can interfere with absorption. By being mindful of these interactions, I can minimize any potential risks and maintain my overall health.I believe my medication routine is working well for me. It can be challenging to keep track of everything, but using a pill planner and setting reminders on my phone helps me stay organized. Additionally, I focus on making lifestyle changes to reduce my reliance on medications whenever possible. My goal is to maintain my health and avoid unnecessary prescriptions by managing my conditions naturally whenever I can.
